{"id":"PKIX-b7d3","title":"Decide whether to move the workspace to edition 2024","description":"## What

The workspace is on edition 2021. Edition 2024 has been available since Rust 1.85 and the MSRV is now 1.88, so the constraint that kept it out is gone.

## What it would unlock

- let chains: `if let Some(a) = x && let Some(b) = y`. These are edition-2024-only, not merely 1.88-only. This workspace has a lot of nested if-let over optional certificate extensions, so it is the change most likely to improve real code here.
- RPIT lifetime capture rules change, which matters if native AFIT is adopted (PKIX-5hoi).
- unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn becomes deny-by-default. Nearly every crate here is forbid(unsafe_code) already, so this only touches pkix-truststore-pkcs11 if and when its FFI lands.

## Why it is a decision and not a chore

Edition 2024 changes semantics, not just syntax:

- Temporary lifetimes in tail expressions shorten, which can change when a lock guard or a borrow is dropped. That is a behaviour change in code that compiles either way.
- `gen` becomes a reserved keyword.
- Changes to match ergonomics around reference patterns.

For a security library the tail-expression-scope change deserves a deliberate look rather than being taken as a side effect of wanting let chains. cargo fix --edition handles the mechanical part and will not flag a behavioural difference it cannot see.

## Also weigh

An edition bump is visible in published metadata and is the kind of thing a downstream consumer notices. It is not breaking -- editions are per-crate -- but it should land as its own change rather than riding along with a feature.

## Acceptance

[ ] Decided for or against, with the reason recorded
[ ] If for: cargo fix --edition per crate, then a read of every tail expression that produces a guard or a borrow
[ ] If for: let chains adopted where they actually simplify existing nested if-let, not mechanically everywhere
[ ] If against: the reason recorded so the question is not reopened every MSRV bump","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"decision","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-24T21:35:36.36873097Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-24T21:35:36.36873097Z"}

{"notes":"DECISION (2026-11-28, Mark): move to edition 2024. Deferred, not done -- recorded here as work.

Grounding measured rather than estimated:

No MSRV cost. Declared rust-version is 1.88; edition 2024 needs 1.85.

Payoff is smaller than this bead's description claims. It says the workspace has 'a lot of nested if-let'; the measured count is 7 directly-nested if-let sites across 6 files. Real, but not a reason on its own.

Risk is smaller still, and the audit list is short. The tail-expression temporary-scope change is the one that deserves care here. 11 candidate sites where a tail expression acquires a guard or borrow, of which 4 are production:

  pkix-zlint-bridge/src/lib.rs:598
  pkix-mta-sts/src/store.rs:343
  pkix-mta-sts/src/store.rs:349
  pkix-mta-sts/src/store.rs:376

All four are the trivially safe shape -- self.policies.read().unwrap().len(), or .get(k).cloned(): acquire, read, return an owned value, no locals whose drop could interact with the guard. Dropping the guard earlier changes nothing. The other 7 are in tests, where the change is harmless.

The argument for doing it now rather than later is timing: the audit surface is 4 sites today and only grows. Deferring does not avoid the review, it enlarges it. unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn becoming deny-by-default is free (everything is forbid(unsafe_code) except the pkix-truststore-pkcs11 stub), and the RPIT capture change matters if native AFIT is taken in PKIX-5hoi.

Work remaining:
  - cargo fix --edition per crate, edition = 2024 in the workspace package section
  - re-read the 4 production sites above and confirm each in the commit message
  - adopt let chains at the 7 nested if-let sites where they actually simplify, not mechanically
  - land as its own commit, not riding along with a feature"}
